categories.title: Profile
categories.description: Build a useful profile without starting from a blank page.

categories.title: Job search
categories.description: Find opportunities and decide which deserve your time.

categories.title: Documents
categories.description: Turn your experience into clear, role-specific materials.

categories.title: Interviews
categories.description: Practice with purpose, then carry what you learn into the next round.

categories.title: Networking
categories.description: Find the right people and prepare a thoughtful message.

categories.title: Growth
categories.description: Choose what to learn and what to build next.

categories.title: Offers
categories.description: Understand the terms and prepare your next conversation.

categories.title: Automation
categories.description: Make recurring work explicit, manageable and reliable.

skills.title: Talk through your experience
skills.summary: Uncover the useful details that your resume leaves out.
skills.whenToUse: Uncover the useful details that your resume leaves out.
inputs: Your existing Lookout profile or resume
The kind of work you want next
steps: Start with your goals and ask one question at a time.
Explore recent work, decisions you made and outcomes you can support.
Review proposed additions before saving them to your profile.
outputs: Proposed profile facts with unresolved details flagged
examples: Help me improve my Lookout profile. Ask one question at a time about my recent work and achievements.
Help me describe my most important project without inventing metrics.
skills.requirements: Your agent needs access to your profile. Unknown metrics should stay unknown; useful qualitative evidence is welcome.

skills.title: Bring in existing documents
skills.summary: Use documents you already have to propose missing profile details.
skills.whenToUse: Use documents you already have to propose missing profile details.
inputs: Your resume, LinkedIn PDF, transcripts or references
Permission to read the documents you choose
steps: Read your current profile before extracting new information.
Identify additions and conflicting dates or titles, with their document sources.
Review a consolidated proposal and save only accepted changes.
outputs: A short list of conflicts to resolve
examples: Use the resume and LinkedIn PDF I provide to propose updates to my Lookout profile.
Compare my transcript with my education section and show what is missing.
skills.requirements: File reading comes from your agent. Some document readers cannot handle DOCX, images or scanned PDFs without text; ask your agent what it can actually read.

skills.title: Find evidence in your portfolio
skills.summary: Find relevant experience in the portfolio and public projects you have linked.
skills.whenToUse: Find relevant experience in the portfolio and public projects you have linked.
inputs: The experience already in your profile
steps: Read the sources you have explicitly provided or linked.
Extract supported technologies, responsibilities and outcomes; deduplicate existing entries.
Show proposed additions and their evidence before saving them.
outputs: New evidence-backed project or experience proposals
examples: Look at the portfolio linked in my profile and suggest experience I have left out.
Find supported skills in my linked GitHub projects and show the evidence before updating anything.
skills.requirements: Browsing is required. Using a library is not evidence that you authored it; unstated dates and results remain blank.

skills.title: Add a project or achievement
skills.summary: Turn completed work into an accurate, useful profile entry.
skills.whenToUse: Turn completed work into an accurate, useful profile entry.
inputs: A project, paper or role description
steps: Read the source and identify your actual contribution.
Draft a concise entry in the appropriate section and check for duplicates.
Let you review the facts before updating your profile.
outputs: A proposed project, publication or work entry
examples: Help me add my finished project to my profile. Separate what I built from the tools I used.
Turn this internship description into accurate resume bullets and ask about missing evidence.
skills.requirements: Changes use Lookout's existing profile tools. Added facts still need your review and verification.

skills.title: Find relevant jobs
skills.summary: Search your chosen sources for roles that fit your goals.
skills.whenToUse: Search your chosen sources for roles that fit your goals.
inputs: Your search preferences and target sources
steps: Check which sources your agent can actually access.
Find relevant listings, deduplicate them and verify official employer postings.
Save supported opportunities in Lookout and explain material gaps or access failures.
examples: Search my saved sources for new backend roles that match my active preferences.
Find internships with strong systems work and explain what still needs verification.
skills.requirements: Browsing or a supported scanner is required. A saved source alone does not mean automatic scanning is active.

skills.title: Quickly check a job
skills.summary: Get a first-pass fit check before spending time on a full evaluation.
skills.whenToUse: Get a first-pass fit check before spending time on a full evaluation.
inputs: A job link or pasted description
steps: Read the actual posting and check obvious blockers.
Compare the role with your goals and strongest evidence.
Return a concise proceed, investigate or skip recommendation.
examples: Quickly triage this role against my profile. Is it worth a deeper look?
Check these three job descriptions for obvious blockers before evaluating them fully.
skills.requirements: Your agent needs real job text and profile context. A preliminary score is not a prediction of hiring success.

skills.title: Evaluate a role in depth
skills.summary: Understand the role, your evidence, the gaps and a sensible application strategy.
skills.whenToUse: Understand the role, your evidence, the gaps and a sensible application strategy.
inputs: A live job posting or complete JD
steps: Summarize the role and match important requirements to concrete evidence.
Assess level, compensation context, constraints and posting signals.
Explain the recommendation, document changes and preparation priorities.
examples: Evaluate this role using my Lookout profile and resume. Show evidence for each important requirement.
Explain why this job is a strong or weak fit and what I should verify before applying.
skills.requirements: Browsing is needed for current posting and company facts. Use your own priorities rather than preset seniority defaults.

skills.title: Compare opportunities
skills.summary: Compare roles using the tradeoffs that matter to you.
skills.whenToUse: Compare roles using the tradeoffs that matter to you.
inputs: Two or more postings or saved opportunities
steps: Agree the dimensions that matter: work, growth, compensation, location and timing.
Compare each opportunity with evidence and explicit unknowns.
Show the tradeoffs and recommend what to investigate next.
examples: Compare these two saved opportunities using my priorities, including learning and work-life balance.
Which of these internships deserves a conversation before I decide?
skills.requirements: The comparison depends on available evidence; missing salary or team details should not be guessed.

skills.title: Research a company
skills.summary: Learn enough about the company and team to ask better questions.
skills.whenToUse: Learn enough about the company and team to ask better questions.
inputs: Company name and role or team
A specific decision you want to inform
steps: Research current products, strategy, engineering work and recent developments.
Separate sourced observations from interpretations.
Connect the findings to your experience, application angle and questions.
examples: Research this company for my application. Focus on engineering culture and what the team is building.
Prepare a company brief before my recruiter call, with sources and useful questions.
skills.requirements: Requires browsing. Keep dates and uncertainty visible; public information may not establish a specific team's practices.

skills.title: Expand your job-title search
skills.summary: Find relevant role titles you may not know to search for.
skills.whenToUse: Find relevant role titles you may not know to search for.
steps: Read the evidence behind your experience.
Suggest adjacent titles with a reason and likely fit tradeoffs.
Review additions or removals before changing search preferences.
outputs: An explanation of which skills transfer
examples: Suggest adjacent job titles supported by my profile that my search may be missing.
Would platform engineering or developer infrastructure be a sensible expansion for me?
skills.requirements: Suggestions do not automatically change your filters. Keep seniority and eligibility constraints explicit.

skills.title: Search in another language or market
skills.summary: Adapt a search to a market while keeping language and location separate.
skills.whenToUse: Adapt a search to a market while keeping language and location separate.
inputs: Preferred output language and known work authorization
steps: Confirm the market, output language and your actual constraints.
Use relevant regional guidance to evaluate location, language, compensation and application conventions.
Verify current official rules when they affect the decision; do not infer eligibility.
outputs: A list of facts to verify
examples: Search for software roles in Germany and explain the results in English. Check language and sponsorship requirements.
Help me search in Singapore and write my application materials in English.
Evaluate this French job posting and explain the result in French.
skills.requirements: Browsing is needed for current market facts. This guide supplies language and regional context, not a certified translation or immigration determination.

skills.title: Tailor your resume
skills.summary: Emphasize the experience most relevant to one role.
skills.whenToUse: Emphasize the experience most relevant to one role.
inputs: Your resume or verified profile facts
steps: Extract the role's important requirements and vocabulary.
Rewrite the summary and reorder supported bullets without adding experience.
Show the tailored draft and any missing evidence for your review.
examples: Tailor my resume for this application using only experience I can support.
Rewrite my summary and reorder my bullets for this job. Show what changed.
skills.requirements: Text drafting works through your agent. Reading a PDF and producing a downloadable file depend on its tools.

skills.title: Create a resume PDF
skills.summary: Prepare a readable resume document tailored to a role.
skills.whenToUse: Prepare a readable resume document tailored to a role.
inputs: A target role and preferred document style
steps: Prepare evidence-backed content and review claims.
Use an available document renderer to produce selectable text and readable structure.
Inspect the final output, then register a new private version when upload tools are available.
outputs: A resume PDF when rendering is available
examples: Create a clean PDF resume for this application and check that its text is selectable.
Use my reviewed resume draft to create a new document version, keeping the original.
skills.requirements: Your agent needs a document renderer. An available renderer must be checked before promising a downloadable file.

skills.title: Check ATS readability
skills.summary: Check document structure and keyword coverage without pretending to predict an employer's ATS.
skills.whenToUse: Check document structure and keyword coverage without pretending to predict an employer's ATS.
inputs: Your resume document or renderable source
A JD if you want keyword coverage
steps: Check text extraction, standard headings, columns and contact placement.
Compare supported keywords with the role when requested.
Explain issues and proposed fixes; keep structure and fit separate.
examples: Check this resume for ATS readability and explain each issue.
Compare keyword coverage with this role without adding skills I do not have.
skills.requirements: Automated structural scoring needs an available checker and compatible source. A clean structure is not an employer pass guarantee.

skills.title: Write a cover letter
skills.summary: Create a specific letter grounded in the role, company and your actual work.
skills.whenToUse: Create a specific letter grounded in the role, company and your actual work.
inputs: A job posting and your resume
steps: Research the company when access is available.
Choose an angle: why this company, its problems, your approach and tone.
Review the draft before formatting or exporting it.
examples: Draft a concise cover letter for this role. Ask me about my motivation before finalizing it.
Make this cover letter more specific using my real projects and the company's work.
skills.requirements: Company research requires browsing. PDF export needs a renderer; drafting never submits an application.

skills.title: Draft an application email
skills.summary: Prepare a clear application email with the right attachments.
skills.whenToUse: Prepare a clear application email with the right attachments.
inputs: Recipient and the documents you plan to attach
steps: Identify the application purpose and supported fit points.
Draft a subject, concise body and appropriate contact block.
List required attachments and leave sending to you.
examples: Draft an application email for this role with a subject and attachment checklist.
Help me send my resume to this recruiter: prepare the email, but do not send it.
skills.requirements: Recipient details must be supplied or verified. This skill prepares a draft; it does not connect an email service.

skills.title: Export a LaTeX resume
skills.summary: Prepare a portable LaTeX resume for your preferred template or Overleaf.
skills.whenToUse: Prepare a portable LaTeX resume for your preferred template or Overleaf.
inputs: Template preferences and the target role
steps: Prepare truthful tailored content.
Create compatible LaTeX source and preserve a clean structure.
Compile and inspect it only if an available tool supports that output.
outputs: A PDF when compilation is available
examples: Create an Overleaf-ready LaTeX version of my reviewed resume.
Adapt my resume content to a simple LaTeX layout and show me the source.
skills.requirements: Compilation depends on your agent's tools. Opening this manual does not install TeX or a rendering engine.

skills.title: Research an interview
skills.summary: Prepare for a company's actual process and the role you are discussing.
skills.whenToUse: Prepare for a company's actual process and the role you are discussing.
inputs: Round type, interviewer and known process details
steps: Research the company and likely process, clearly labeling unverified reports.
Connect likely topics to your experience and gaps.
Prepare questions, talking points and a focused next step.
outputs: Likely topics and questions to ask
examples: Research my upcoming interview for this application and distinguish official facts from candidate reports.
Help me prepare questions for the hiring manager based on this team's work.
skills.requirements: Requires browsing for fresh company intelligence. Public candidate reports are observations, not a guaranteed interview script.

skills.title: Build an interview preparation plan
skills.summary: Use the time you have to prepare the most important topics.
skills.whenToUse: Use the time you have to prepare the most important topics.
steps: Confirm the deadline and current preparation budget.
Prioritize topics, stories and practice for this round.
Update the existing Lookout preparation plan while preserving completed tasks.
examples: Build a preparation plan for this application using my saved daily budget and confirmed interview date.
I have three evenings before my interview. Help me prioritize what to practice.
skills.requirements: Use existing Lookout planner tools when available. Uncertain dates stay unscheduled; planning is not task completion.

skills.title: Practice an interview
skills.summary: Practice one question at a time with feedback grounded in your experience.
skills.whenToUse: Practice one question at a time with feedback grounded in your experience.
steps: Choose the round and practice style.
Ask one question, wait for your answer, then give specific feedback.
Keep track of weak areas and stronger evidence-backed answers.
examples: Run a mock backend interview. Ask one question at a time and give feedback after I answer.
Practice a recruiter screen using my profile. Challenge vague answers without inventing better facts.
skills.requirements: This is an interactive conversation with your agent. Saving a practice transcript depends on available storage tools and your permission.

skills.title: Build your interview story bank
skills.summary: Develop a small set of truthful stories you can adapt to behavioral questions.
skills.whenToUse: Develop a small set of truthful stories you can adapt to behavioral questions.
steps: Choose a concrete experience and clarify your role.
Describe situation, task, action, result and reflection using supported facts.
Identify the competencies it demonstrates and how to adapt it without embellishment.
examples: Help me build five interview stories from my real work. Start with a technical challenge.
Turn this experience into a STAR story and flag any result I have not supported.
skills.requirements: Keep stories private unless you choose to share. Lookout's saved-answer library is not automatic permission to reuse every story in an application.

skills.title: Debrief an interview
skills.summary: Capture what happened while it is fresh and improve the next round.
skills.whenToUse: Capture what happened while it is fresh and improve the next round.
steps: Record your observations without guessing the interviewer's judgment.
Identify strong answers, gaps and better-supported examples.
Prepare next-round actions and add relevant notes through available Lookout tools.
examples: Debrief my interview with me. Ask what happened before deciding what I should improve.
Help me capture the questions I was asked and make a plan for the next round.
skills.requirements: Unknown outcomes remain unknown. A debrief does not publish an interview report to a Circle.

skills.title: Review interview warning signs
skills.summary: Reflect on observed interview behavior and mismatches before deciding what to ask next.
skills.whenToUse: Reflect on observed interview behavior and mismatches before deciding what to ask next.
inputs: The JD and relevant offer or scope details
steps: Identify concrete statements and events.
Separate isolated observations from repeated patterns or corroborated mismatches.
Prepare neutral follow-up questions and identify anything requiring current official guidance.
examples: Review my interview notes for scope or compensation mismatches. Separate facts from interpretations.
Help me decide what to clarify after these inconsistent answers from the interview panel.
skills.requirements: Your agent must not infer motives or issue legal conclusions. Sensitive jurisdiction-specific claims require current verification.

skills.title: Find people to contact
skills.summary: Identify a relevant recruiter, hiring manager or team peer and a suitable approach.
skills.whenToUse: Identify a relevant recruiter, hiring manager or team peer and a suitable approach.
inputs: Your existing contacts and genuine shared context
steps: Check saved contacts before cold research.
Verify a person's relevance and choose a contact-appropriate angle.
Use Lookout's outreach guide to draft a specific message for your review.
examples: Check whether I already know someone at this company, then suggest who to contact.
Find a relevant team contact for this role and prepare a short LinkedIn note.
skills.requirements: Research requires browsing. A public profile does not establish a relationship, and this skill never sends a message.

skills.title: Prepare a follow-up
skills.summary: Choose a reasonable follow-up and prepare the message.
skills.whenToUse: Choose a reasonable follow-up and prepare the message.
steps: Confirm what was sent, when and whether there has been a response.
Choose an appropriate follow-up using the real timeline.
Draft the message and distinguish a draft from a sent follow-up.
examples: Help me follow up on this application using the actual dates in my timeline.
Draft a follow-up to this recruiter based on our last message. Do not send it.
skills.requirements: A sent message or submission must be established before drafting a chase-up. A reminder does not mean delivery is configured.

skills.title: Understand an employer reply
skills.summary: Separate a real process update from recruiting noise and decide what to do.
skills.whenToUse: Separate a real process update from recruiting noise and decide what to do.
inputs: The reply you choose to provide
steps: Read the message and match it to the correct application.
Classify the update and extract only supported dates and actions.
Propose or record an attributable milestone using available tools; keep submission evidence separate.
examples: Explain this recruiter email and identify the next action. Keep ambiguous dates unresolved.
Match this interview invitation to the correct application and propose a timeline update.
skills.requirements: Pasting a reply works without an inbox connection. Continuous monitoring needs authorized email access in your agent's runtime.

skills.title: Identify recurring skill gaps
skills.summary: Find the gaps that repeatedly matter for your target roles.
skills.whenToUse: Find the gaps that repeatedly matter for your target roles.
inputs: Past evaluations or a set of job descriptions
Your current evidence and target roles
steps: Collect missing and partial requirements across the available roles.
Separate genuinely missing skills from skills with weak evidence.
Prioritize the gaps and explain what data is too thin to judge.
examples: Find recurring skill gaps across these job descriptions and my profile.
Which requirements keep blocking roles I want, and which could I prove with better examples?
skills.requirements: Cross-role analysis needs actual evaluations or supplied JDs. Do not invent rejection reasons or claim unavailable history was analyzed.

skills.title: Plan what to learn next
skills.summary: Turn a meaningful skill gap into a manageable learning plan.
skills.whenToUse: Turn a meaningful skill gap into a manageable learning plan.
inputs: A target skill or gap analysis
Your time budget and preferred resources
steps: Choose a concrete outcome that supports your target work.
Find current, preferably free resources and verify their relevance.
Propose an ordered plan with practice and a demonstrable result.
examples: Make a four-week learning plan for the most important gap in my target roles.
Find free resources and a small practice project to strengthen my database systems evidence.
skills.requirements: Current resource recommendations require browsing. Preparation time and completed work should reflect your actual schedule and reports.

skills.title: Evaluate a course or certification
skills.summary: Decide whether a learning opportunity is worth your time.
skills.whenToUse: Decide whether a learning opportunity is worth your time.
inputs: Your goals, current knowledge and alternatives
steps: Review content, prerequisites, effort and cost.
Assess role alignment, hiring signal, risks and opportunity cost.
Recommend whether to pursue it and what artifact would make it useful.
examples: Evaluate this certification against my career goals and the time it would take.
Would this course help more than building a project for the roles I want?
skills.requirements: Browsing is needed for current course details and prices. Recommendations should not assume a certificate guarantees employment.

skills.title: Evaluate a portfolio project
skills.summary: Choose a project that demonstrates skills your target roles need.
skills.whenToUse: Choose a project that demonstrates skills your target roles need.
inputs: A project idea or existing repository
Target role requirements and your time budget
steps: Assess relevance, uniqueness, demo potential, metrics and effort.
Define a bounded MVP that demonstrates real technical decisions.
Explain how to turn the work into evidence and interview material.
examples: Evaluate this project idea for backend roles and suggest a realistic MVP.
What should I build to demonstrate distributed systems skills with a two-week budget?
skills.requirements: Estimates are planning assumptions. Proposed metrics and outcomes are not accomplishments until you measure them.

skills.title: Compare compensation
skills.summary: Understand desired, advertised and offered compensation without mixing unlike figures.
skills.whenToUse: Understand desired, advertised and offered compensation without mixing unlike figures.
inputs: Actual JD, recruiter or offer figures
Currency, pay period and known components
steps: Separate base, bonus, equity and benefits, retaining sources and dates.
Compare desired, advertised and actual numbers on compatible terms.
Highlight unknowns, conflicting figures and useful clarification questions.
examples: Compare my target compensation with these offer figures. Keep base, equity and bonus separate.
Compare these two offers without treating an uncertain equity value as guaranteed cash.
skills.requirements: Calculations need compatible currency and pay periods. Do not guess exchange rates or interpret a historical range as an offer.

skills.title: Prepare a negotiation
skills.summary: Prepare a thoughtful compensation conversation grounded in your actual leverage.
skills.whenToUse: Prepare a thoughtful compensation conversation grounded in your actual leverage.
inputs: Any real alternatives you choose to disclose
steps: Clarify the ask, fallback and terms that matter.
Connect the request to supported achievements and current evidence.
Draft talking points and practice responses to likely objections.
outputs: An opening message and practice responses
examples: Help me prepare a negotiation using this offer and my actual achievements.
Practice a conversation about base salary and flexibility without inventing competing offers.
skills.requirements: Your agent prepares the conversation. It does not contact the employer or accept terms on your behalf.

skills.title: Understand an offer or contract
skills.summary: Prepare to discuss terms, gaps and questions with the employer or an adviser.
skills.whenToUse: Prepare to discuss terms, gaps and questions with the employer or an adviser.
inputs: The offer or contract you choose to provide
Your location and earlier written promises
steps: Describe the terms and notable omissions in plain language.
Compare the document with what was actually promised.
Separate employer questions from questions for a qualified local adviser.
outputs: An employer and adviser question list
examples: Walk me through this offer and list questions for the employer and a qualified adviser.
Compare this written offer with the recruiter notes I provide and flag differences.
skills.requirements: Private document access is required. This is reading and preparation, not a legal determination or acceptance of the offer.

skills.title: Plan a recurring search
skills.summary: Make a recurring job search explicit before turning it on.
skills.whenToUse: Make a recurring job search explicit before turning it on.
inputs: An agent runtime that can schedule work
steps: Agree what each run should search, save and report.
Check runtime scheduling capability and explain any missing setup.
Create a schedule only when authorized and supported, then confirm its actual state.
outputs: A verified schedule only if the runtime supports it
examples: Help me set up a weekday job search at 9am America/New_York. Check scheduling support before enabling it.
Plan a scan every three days and tell me exactly what still needs setup.
skills.requirements: Lookout settings do not activate a scheduler. Cron, launchd or another runtime may be used as appropriate; source recipes are reference material, not automatically installed jobs.

skills.title: Plan recurring follow-up reviews
skills.summary: Review overdue applications regularly and prepare useful drafts.
skills.whenToUse: Review overdue applications regularly and prepare useful drafts.
inputs: A review cadence and notification preference
steps: Define which applications qualify for review.
Check whether the runtime can read the necessary history and schedule a sweep.
Prepare drafts on supported runs and report only meaningful changes.
examples: Plan a weekly review of applications that need a follow-up. Draft messages, but never send them automatically.
Check what I need to enable a Friday follow-up sweep that respects quiet mode.
skills.requirements: Scheduling and delivery require working runtime capabilities. Recurring review never grants permission to send outreach.

skills.title: Review what is working
skills.summary: Look for useful patterns in your own recorded search outcomes.
skills.whenToUse: Look for useful patterns in your own recorded search outcomes.
steps: Summarize the funnel and the evidence available.
Compare outcomes by role, score or channel without assuming causation.
Suggest questions and preference changes for your review.
examples: Review my recorded search outcomes and identify patterns without guessing why I was rejected.
Which parts of my search deserve a closer look, given the data I actually have?
skills.requirements: Small samples and pending outcomes must stay visible. Your agent needs access to the relevant history and calculation tools.

skills.title: Check your fit scoring
skills.summary: Check whether past fit scores have been useful in your own search.
skills.whenToUse: Check whether past fit scores have been useful in your own search.
steps: Check that scores and outcomes refer to the same applications.
Compare score bands while retaining pending cases and sample-size limits.
Explain whether evidence supports a pattern and leave scoring changes to you.
examples: Do my recorded fit scores predict interviews in my search? Say if there is too little data.
Review high-scored rejections with me without automatically changing my scoring rules.
skills.requirements: Needs real recorded scores and outcomes. Do not fabricate statistics or silently tune global scoring from a small sample.
